title: memory-pressure-incident-triage-and-recovery-playbook-2026
author: Nadia Gomez
content:
Summary:

This runbook describes detection, triage, mitigation, and recovery procedures for GPU and host memory pressure incidents affecting the Redwood serving runtime. It centralizes observable signals, automated mitigations, manual steps, rollback guidance, and post-incident analysis templates. It is intended for on-call SREs, runtime engineers, and the serving runtime owners.

Scope and intent:
- Applies to production and pre-prod clusters running the runtime (hosted and dedicated).
- Covers transient memory spikes, sustained memory leaks, KV cache bloat, and OOMs that surface as request failures, elevated tail latency, or node instability.
- Does NOT replace component-specific leak-fix investigations (those belong in an RCA). This is an operational triage and recovery playbook.

Key signals (primary metrics and thresholds):
- gpu_memory_utilization_pct > 92% (sustained for > 60s) => warning
- cuda_free_bytes < 0.1 * cuda_total_bytes (free < 10%) => critical
- host_mem_free_pct < 8% => critical
- node_oom_kills > 0 in last 5m => critical
- kvcache_eviction_rate == 0 while kvcache_size growing => suspicious
- request_rejection_rate > 0.5% & tail_p95_latency > SLO => operational impact

Recommended alert definitions (examples):
- ALERT RuntimeGpuMemoryPressure
  - expr: avg_over_time(gpu_memory_utilization_pct[1m]) > 92
  - for: 1m
  - severity: page

- ALERT HostMemoryExhaustion
  - expr: avg_over_time(node_memory_free_percent[2m]) < 8
  - for: 2m
  - severity: page

Quick detection checklist (what to look at first):
1) Is the alert noisy or isolated? Check cluster scope and pod cardinality.
2) Are requests failing with OOM or CUDA errors? Check logs for "OutOfMemoryError", "cudaErrorUnknown", "CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED".
3) Correlate with recent deploys/rollouts or model variant switches in the last 10 minutes.
4) Confirm whether KV cache warmup or bulk-replay jobs are running.

On-call escalation matrix (who to call):
- Primary: runtime-oncall (pager duty) -> owns immediate remediation
- Secondary: serving-platform (Slack: #serving-platform)
- Tertiary: runtime-kernel-team (for suspected kernel/cuda issues)

Automated mitigations (automatically triggered by the control plane):
- Soft eviction: decremented KVCACHE retention per tenant by 20% for 2 minutes. This frees pinned prefixes preferentially.
- Request shedder: temporarily reject low-priority background requests and batch-jobs for 30s.
- Model fallback: route to smaller model variant with identical interface (e.g., 13B->7B) for impacted routes if configured.
- Slot reduction: reduce per-tenant concurrency slot allocation by 25% to avoid head-of-line memory bloat.

When automated mitigations run, on-call must verify impact within 60–120s and whether further manual action is required.

Manual triage and remediation steps (ordered):
1) Triage & scope
   - Identify impacted nodes via alert dashboard: query node labels and pod assignments for the high-mem nodes.
   - Grafana queries to run:
     - gpu_memory_by_node: avg(gpu_memory_alloc_bytes) by (node)
     - kvcache_size_by_tenant: sum(kvcache_bytes) by (tenant)
     - recent_deploys: increase(time() - deploy_timestamp_seconds < 600)

2) Immediate mitigation (safe, low-risk first)
   - Trigger soft eviction manually if automated path not already run: POST /admin/evict?scope=soft&fraction=0.2
   - Disable non-critical background jobs: apply label "no-batch" to pods via kubectl or patch the job controller.
   - Flip model-route to fallback variant for the tenant: use routing API -> PATCH /routes/{route}/variant -> {"variant":"fallback-small"}

3) Step-up mitigation (if memory continues rising)
   - Drain requests from the most memory-taxing nodes: kubectl cordon && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force <node>
   - Evacuate long-lived sessions: signal runtime to gracefully terminate sessions with > N cached tokens. (runtime admin CLI: runtime-admin sessions terminate --idle-gt 3600)
   - Reduce per-request max_sequence_length via runtime config for affected routes.

4) Emergency mitigation (if OOMs continuing or node instability)
   - Scale down concurrency aggressively for the cluster or move tenants to lower-memory pools.
   - Power-cycle affected GPU nodes through the node pool API (last resort).

Rollback and recovery guidance:
- If the incident started with a deploy/rollout, immediately roll back the deploy using the canary matrix in the deployment dashboard. Record rollback ID and time.
- After memory metrics stabilize (gpu_memory_utilization_pct < 65% for 5m and host_mem_free_pct > 20%), reverse mitigations in reverse order: uncordon nodes, restore background jobs, re-enable higher-concurrency slots, and re-route traffic to primary model variants gradually (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 5m observation window).

Root cause hypotheses and evidence checklist (collect before altering state):
- Memory leak in kernel-level allocator: evidence = steadily increasing GPU reserved bytes even with low request rate, kernel update in last 24h.
- KV cache pinning: evidence = kvcache_size growing with zero eviction_rate & tenants with long-running sessions.
- Bursty large-batch traffic (client-side): evidence = sudden spike in batch_size distribution and request aggregation metrics.
- Model switch oscillation causing multiple variants to instantiate simultaneously: evidence = near-simultaneous model_load events and peak in model_startup_allocations.
- Driver / CUDA bug: evidence = correlated driver update + node-level coredumps or CUDA errors across heterogeneous hardware.

Forensic commands and useful log snippets:
- kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector status.phase=Running -l service=runtime --all-namespaces
- journalctl -u runtime.service --since "10 minutes ago" | grep -E "OutOfMemory|cudaError|CUBLAS"
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.total,memory.free,memory.used --format=csv -l 1
- runtime-admin metrics dump --node <node> --out /tmp/metrics.json

Suggested dashboards and panels to check:
- Cluster memory overview (node+gpu) – panel: node_free_pct, gpu_free_bytes
- Top tenants by GPU memory (table) – kvcache size, session count, recent model loads
- Request pipeline telemetry – queue_depth, batch_size_distribution, p95/p99 latency
- Recent driver and kernel deploy timeline overlay

Playbook of short CLI snippets (examples):
- Force soft eviction for tenant 'acme':
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://controlplane.internal/admin/evict?tenant=acme&scope=soft&fraction=0.25
- Drain a node safely:
  kubectl cordon gpu-node-17
  kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
- Patch a route to smaller variant:
  curl -X PATCH -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://controlplane.internal/api/routes/my-chat-route -d '{"variant":"13b-to-7b-fallback"}'

Owner and responsibilities table (informal table):
- Incident owner: runtime-oncall (page) => triage, run mitigations, escalate.
- Kernel/pool issues: runtime-kernel-team => kernel-level fixes, kernel rollback.
- KV cache behavior: serving-platform => cache policies, eviction tuning.
- Post-incident RCA: runtime-techlead => lead investigation and publish RCA.

Post-incident checklist and RCA template (to run within 48h):
1) Save all monitoring data slices (5m before start, during incident, 30m after) and upload to incident folder.
2) List timeline with exact timestamps for deploys, mitigations, and observed metric changes.
3) Hypotheses considered and tests run (include commands and results).
4) Root cause conclusion and long-term mitigations (code fixes, config changes, alert tuning).
5) Action owners and deadlines.

Example mitigation proposals (long term):
- KVCACHE adaptive eviction policy: implement per-tenant LRU aging + memory headroom target.
- Slot-aware allocation: use per-GPU soft quotas and proactive slot shedding when headroom < 20%.
- Memory-safety CI job: inject synthetic leaks in a staging harness ("oom-injector-simulator") to validate auto-eviction and draining behavior.
- Runtime memory accounting improvements: instrument allocator to report per-session and per-model allocation breakdowns.

Related pages and references:
- runtime-telemetry-schema (dashboard link)
- kernel-and-scheduling/preemption-aware-batch-slicing-spec-2026
- runbooks/cold-start-warmup-strategies-and-entropy-reduction-2025

Appendix: quick decision table (text table)
| Symptom | First action | When to escalate | Likely owner |
|---------|--------------|-------------------|--------------|
| Rapid GPU mem rise but requests normal | Soft-evict KVCACHE; check for background jobs | If mem stays >90% for 3m | serving-platform |
| Frequent OOM kills | Cordons + drain node; migrate tenants | Immediate page | runtime-kernel-team |
| Model load storms during deploy | Rollback deploy canary; enable model fallback | If reoccurs on rollback -> page | runtime-release |

Contact and runbook updates:
- Keep this doc current: runtime-oncall updates after every major kernel or routing change.
- Add any new remediation commands or endpoints to the Playbook CLI list above.

End of document.
